\begin{theorem}[Characterisation of a one-symbol buffer]
\lean{Turing.cert_tail_test}
\label{Turing.cert_tail_test}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{4}
For a Boolean word $w$, the cell at integer position $|w|-1$ contains `true` and the
cell at position $|w|-2$ is blank if and only if $w$ is the one-symbol word
$[\text{true}]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Certificate verdict machine]
\lean{Turing.certVerdictTM}
\label{Turing.certVerdictTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM}
For a natural number $k$ and a designated work-tape index $c$ among the $k$ tapes,
define a three-state Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols. It starts in state $0$;
in state $0$ it moves the head on tape $c$ one cell left and enters state $1$. In state
$1$, if the scanned symbol on tape $c$ is true, it again moves that head one cell left
and enters state $2$; otherwise it outputs false and halts. In state $2$, it outputs
true exactly when the scanned cell on tape $c$ is blank, and halts. In every step the
input head stays put, and no work-tape cell is written.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Three-step certificate verdict]
\lean{Turing.certVerdict_run}
\label{Turing.certVerdict_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.certVerdictTM, Turing.cert_tail_test}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ be one of the
$k$ tape slots. Suppose a configuration $d$ has state $0$, tape $c$ contains the word
$w$ starting at cell $0$ and is blank elsewhere, and its head on that tape is at cell
$|w|$. After three steps of the certificate-verdict machine from $d$, the machine is
halted and its output is $d$'s original output followed by the bit that is true exactly
when $w=[\mathrm{true}]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Captured Tape Contents and Head Position]
\lean{Turing.cert_capture_fields}
\label{Turing.cert_capture_fields}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.embedSilentCfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m,k$ be natural numbers, let $S$ be a state type, and let $x$ be a Boolean input
word. Let $\iota$ inject the $m$ tape indices into the $k$ tape indices, and let
$\mathrm{cap}$ be a tape index outside its image. For any tape contents, tape-head
positions, Boolean words $\mathrm{pre}$ and $\mathrm{out}_0$, and configuration $d$ on
$m$ tapes, the embedded configuration has on tape $\mathrm{cap}$ the buffer storing
$\mathrm{pre}$ followed by the output of $d$, and its head on that tape is positioned at
the length of that concatenated word.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Certificate core machine construction]
\lean{Turing.certCoreTM}
\label{Turing.certCoreTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.certVerdictTM, Turing.embedSilentRetTM, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM}
Given a finite Turing machine $P$ over the Boolean alphabet with $P.k$ work tapes, an
injection from the indices of $1+P.k$ tapes into the indices of $k$ tapes, and a
designated tape index among those $k$ tapes, the construction produces a finite Boolean
Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and state set
$((P.State\times\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\})\sqcup\{\ast\})\sqcup\{0,1,2\}$. Its
transition machine is obtained by composing the embedded virtual-host emission machine
for $P$ with the certificate-verdict machine on the designated tape, using the unit
state and parameter $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded certificate run]
\lean{Turing.certCore_run}
\label{Turing.certCore_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM.exists_first_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.certCoreTM, Turing.certVerdictTM, Turing.certVerdict_run, Turing.cert_capture_fields, Turing.embedSilentCfg, Turing.embedSilentRetTM, Turing.embedSilentRetTM_run, Turing.seamCompTM_run_ofCfg, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{6}
Let $P$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols and $k_P$ work tapes, and
let $k$ be a natural number. Let $\iota$ be an injection from the $1+k_P$ tape slots
into the $k$ tape slots, and choose a slot $c$ outside its image. For Boolean words
$x,y$, let $d$ be a configuration of $P$ on input $x$ with a nonhalting state. Choose a
Boolean tag satisfying the boundary-tag condition at $d$’s input-head position, a
position $p$ among the $|y|+2$ positions, and arbitrary contents and head positions for
the $k$ tapes. If the run of $P$ from $d$ is halted at time $D$, then the certificate
machine, started from the configuration built from these data, is halted at some time
$t\le D+4$; its output is the one-symbol word whose symbol is true exactly when the
output of $P$ at time $D$ is the one-symbol word $[\mathrm{true}]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cutting a Machine Call]
\lean{Turing.cert_call_cut}
\label{Turing.cert_call_cut}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.seamReleaseTM, Turing.seamReleaseTM_firstReturn}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a finite state set, and let $M$ be a $k$-tape
Boolean machine with states in $S$. Suppose that for every parameter $a$ there is a time
$t$ no greater than a prescribed natural-number budget, with $t>0$, such that the run
from state $\mathrm{en}$ and tape words $\mathrm{before}(a)$ does not visit state
$\mathrm{ex}$ at any positive time strictly before $t$, and at time $t$ reaches state
$\mathrm{ex}$ with tape words $\mathrm{after}(a)$. Then there exist a finite state set
and a $k$-tape Boolean machine, together with start and finish states, such that for
every $a$ some time within the same budget reaches the finish state with tape words
$\mathrm{after}(a)$ from the start state and words $\mathrm{before}(a)$, and the finish
state is not visited at any earlier time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Embedding Tape Words]
\lean{Turing.cert_embed_words}
\label{Turing.cert_embed_words}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_pos, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_tape, Turing.embedEmitTM_frame}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $S$ be a state set, and let $y$ be a Boolean
input word. Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine with $m$ work tapes over the Boolean
alphabet, let $ho:\text{Fin}(m)\to\text{Fin}(k)$ be an injection, and let $q\in S$. For
families of Boolean words $w$ on the $m$ tapes and $f,t$ on the $k$ tapes, suppose
$t(\rho(i))=w(i)$ for every $i$ and $t(j)=f(j)$ for every $j$ outside the image of
$\rho$. Then the configuration formed from the words $w$ in state $q$, with the words
$f$ on tapes outside the embedded indices, all work-tape heads at cell zero, and empty
output, equals the configuration formed from the words $t$ in state $q$ on input $y$,
with all work-tape heads at cell zero and empty output.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Embedded machine call]
\lean{Turing.cert_embed_call}
\label{Turing.cert_embed_call}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.cert_embed_words, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{3}
Let $y$ be a Boolean input word, let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $m$ work
tapes over the Boolean alphabet and state set $S$, and let $\iota$ inject the $m$ tape
indices into the $k$ tape indices. Choose entry and exit states
$\mathrm{en},\mathrm{ex}\in S$, local tape-word assignments
$L_0,L_1:\mathrm{Fin}(m)\to\mathrm{List}(\mathrm{Bool})$, and larger tape-word
assignments $B_0,B_1:\mathrm{Fin}(k)\to\mathrm{List}(\mathrm{Bool})$. Suppose
$B_0(\iota(i))=L_0(i)$ and $B_1(\iota(i))=L_1(i)$ for every $i<m$, and $B_1(j)=B_0(j)$
for every $j$ outside the image of $\iota$. If the run of $M$ from the configuration
with input $y$, state $\mathrm{en}$, and tape words $L_0$ reaches the configuration with
state $\mathrm{ex}$ and tape words $L_1$ after $t$ steps, and its state is not
$\mathrm{ex}$ at any time $u<t$, then the machine obtained by embedding $M$ into the $k$
tapes while retaining its output tape reaches state $\mathrm{ex}$ with tape words $B_1$
after $t$ steps, and its state is not $\mathrm{ex}$ at any time $u<t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sequential Composition of Machine Runs]
\lean{Turing.cert_seq}
\label{Turing.cert_seq}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.seamCompTM_firstReturn, Turing.seamCompTM_run}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ and $N$ be Boolean machines with the same number $k$ of work tapes and state
sets $S$ and $U$, respectively, with decidable equality on $S$. Suppose the run of $M$
from state $\mathrm{en}$ and tape assignment $w_0$ reaches state $\mathrm{ex}$ with
assignment $w_1$ after $t_0$ steps, without visiting $\mathrm{ex}$ at any earlier time;
and the run of $N$ from state $\mathrm{start}$ and assignment $w_1$ reaches state
$\mathrm{finish}$ with assignment $w_2$ after $t_1$ steps, without visiting
$\mathrm{finish}$ at any earlier time. Then the machine that runs $M$ until its exit
state and then switches to $N$ reaches the right-hand copy of $\mathrm{finish}$ with
assignment $w_2$ after $t_0+1+t_1$ steps, and does not visit that state at any earlier
time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Word on an Embedded Tape]
\lean{Turing.cert_bank_word}
\label{Turing.cert_bank_word}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $m,k$ be natural numbers with $m>0$, let
$\iota:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\hookrightarrow\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$ be an injection, and let
$\mathrm{frame}$ assign a Boolean word to each of the $k$ tapes, with the empty word on
every tape in the image of $\iota$. For any Boolean word $w$ and every $i<m$, replacing
the contents of tape $\iota(0)$ by $w$ gives the standard assignment on $m$ tapes that
places $w$ on tape zero and the empty word on every other tape.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Turing.cert_silent_words}

into $k$ tape indices, and let $\mathrm{cap}$ be outside the image of $\iota$. Suppose
$d$ is an $m$-tape configuration on Boolean input $y$ whose state is $q$, whose input
head is at position $1$, whose tape contents are the buffers storing $w(\iota(i))$ on
each local tape $i$, whose tape heads are all at position $0$, and whose output is
empty; also suppose $w(\mathrm{cap})$ is empty. Then embedding $d$ with the buffer words
$w$ and zero head positions, and renaming every state to $\mathrm{finish}$, gives the
standard configuration on $k$ tapes with state $\mathrm{finish}$ and tape assignment
$w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Certificate split-word encoding]
\lean{Turing.certSplitWord}
\label{Turing.certSplitWord}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode, Turing.solveSplit}
For natural numbers $C$ and $c$ and a Boolean word $y$, define a word by solving the
split problem with parameters $C$, $c$, and the length of $y$. If the solver returns a
split index $i$, encode the prefix of $y$ of length $i$ together with the suffix
beginning at $i$; if it returns no index, use the empty word.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Length bound for the certificate word]
\lean{Turing.certSplitWord_length}
\label{Turing.certSplitWord_length}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.certSplitWord, Turing.length_pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C,c$ be natural numbers and let $y$ be a finite bit string. Form a word by finding
an $i\le |y|$ satisfying $i+C(i+1)^c=|y|$; if one exists, encode the first $i$ bits of
$y$ together with the remaining suffix using the self-delimiting pair encoding, and
otherwise take the empty word. The resulting word has length at most $2|y|+2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Validity of the certificate split]
\lean{Turing.certSplit_valid}
\label{Turing.certSplit_valid}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.solveSplit}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C,c$ be natural numbers and let $y$ be a Boolean word. If the split solver for
$C,c,|y|$ returns $i$, then the suffix of $y$ after its first $i$ bits has length $C$
times one plus the length of the prefix of those first $i$ bits, raised to the power
$c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of the split language]
\lean{Turing.certSplit_language}
\label{Turing.certSplit_language}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.append_split_unique, Turing.certSplit_valid, Turing.certificateLength_strictMono, Turing.solveSplit}
\difficulty{5}
Let $C,c$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{out}$ map pairs of Boolean words to Boolean
words, and let $y$ be a Boolean word. There exist words $x,u$ with $y=xu$,
$|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$, and $\mathrm{out}(x,u)=[\mathrm{true}]$ if and only if the following
holds: if the split solver for $C,c,|y|$ returns no value, the condition is false; if it
returns $i$, then $\mathrm{out}(y_{<i},y_{\ge i})=[\mathrm{true}]$, where $y_{<i}$ is
the prefix of length $i$ and $y_{\ge i}$ is the remaining suffix.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Certificate guard machine]
\lean{Turing.certGuardTM}
\label{Turing.certGuardTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM}
For a natural number $k$ and a designated work-tape index $j$ among the $k$ tapes,
define a Boolean-state Turing machine that starts in state false. On each transition it
leaves the input head and all work-tape heads in place and writes nothing. If the
scanned cell on tape $j$ is blank, it outputs false and halts; otherwise it outputs
nothing and enters state true, after which it outputs nothing and halts.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[One-step behavior of the certificate guard]
\lean{Turing.certGuard_run}
\label{Turing.certGuard_run}
\leanok

\difficulty{3}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $y$ be a Boolean input word, let $s$ be one of the $k$
tape slots, and let $w$ assign a Boolean word to each slot. From the configuration with
initial state false, input head at position $1$, tape contents given by $w$ starting at
cell $0$, all tape heads at cell $0$, and empty output, after one step the
certificate-guard machine reaches the halted configuration with output
$[\mathrm{false}]$ if $w_s$ is empty; otherwise it reaches the same initial
configuration with state true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded preparation of a virtual-host configuration]
\lean{Turing.cert_prepare_exists}
\label{Turing.cert_prepare_exists}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSnd, Turing.FinTM.exists_installCallTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.cert_bank_word, Turing.cert_call_cut, Turing.cert_embed_call, Turing.cert_seq, Turing.cert_silent_words, Turing.copyTM, Turing.copyTM_run, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedSilentCfg, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.stateWord, Turing.transferTM, Turing.transferTM_run, Turing.vhostBank, Turing.vhostBuffer, Turing.vhostCap, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM}
\difficulty{7}
Let $P$ be a Boolean Turing machine with finitely many states and $P.k$ work tapes, let
$j$ be a work-tape index of $P$, and let $m$ be a positive integer. There exist a
finite-state Boolean Turing machine $D$, a state $e$ of $D$, injections from the $m$
tape indices and from the $1+P.k$ tape indices into the work tapes of $D$, a work-tape
index $c$ outside the image of the latter injection, and a natural number $a$ such that
the following holds. For every Boolean input word $y$ and Boolean words $x,u$, when $D$
starts on input $y$ with the encoding of $(x,u)$ on the tape indexed by the image of $0$
under the first injection and all other work tapes empty, there is a time $t\le
a(|x|+|u|+1)$ at which its configuration has state $e$, input-head position $1$, and
empty output. Its work tapes and head positions agree, under the second injection, with
the virtual-host configuration whose simulated machine is in its initial state on input
$x$, with $u$ on tape $j$, all other simulated work tapes empty, and boundary tag true;
tape $c$ is empty with its head at position $0$, and the remaining tapes and head
positions may be chosen arbitrarily. No earlier configuration in this run has state $e$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Turing.FinTM.exists_certificateShell}

\begin{theorem}[Certificate-shell projection]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.certificateShell_proj}
\label{Turing.FinTM.certificateShell_proj}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.append_split_unique, Turing.certificateLength_strictMono}
\difficulty{4}
Let $C,c$ be nonnegative integers and let $\mathrm{out}$ be any function from pairs of
Boolean words to Boolean words. The set of words $x$ for which some word $u$ has length
$C(|x|+1)^c$ and $x u$ can be written as $x' u'$ with $|u'|=C(|x'|+1)^c$ and
$\mathrm{out}(x',u')=[1]$ equals the set of words $x$ for which some word $u$ has length
$C(|x|+1)^c$ and $\mathrm{out}(x,u)=[1]$.
\end{theorem}
